name: Attack telegraph
summary: Enemies show a clear wind-up before an attack becomes dangerous, so the player can react.
what_it_does: An attack that is dangerous on the frame it starts can't be avoided by reacting, only by luck. A telegraph adds a visible wind-up (a pose, a color change, a marked danger zone) for a fixed time before the attack turns on. The wind-up has to be longer than reaction time plus the time the dodge needs.
use_when: Every enemy attack the player is meant to dodge or block.
watch_out: Keep tells consistent: the same wind-up always means the same attack. Very long tells make fights slow.
starting_values: No checked source gives one number. 300 to 600 ms of wind-up is a starting range; it has to cover reaction time plus the dodge.
prompt:
Add telegraphs to enemy attacks.
- Before an attack becomes active, play a 450 ms wind-up: change the enemy's color or pose and mark the danger area.
- The attack can't deal damage during the wind-up.
- Use the same tell every time for the same attack.
- Randomize when attacks start, not how long the tell lasts.

Acceptance checks:
1. Every attack comes after a visible 450 ms wind-up.
2. A player who reacts to the tell can always avoid the attack.
3. No damage happens during the wind-up.
